title: Provable Bounds for the Learnability of Sample-Compressible Families from Noisy Samples
claim: A simple structure in the data distribution lets a few samples near key points reconstruct the whole distribution.
layout: single panel, Gaussian curve over a sample axis, shaded neighborhoods with double-arrows
description: A single black Gaussian density curve labeled N(μ, σ²) is drawn over a horizontal axis, with a vertical y-axis arrow at the left. Two light-grey vertical bands sit on the curve's shoulders, one on each side of the mean, at roughly μ−σ and μ+σ. Each band is marked with a black double-headed arrow and the label 2ε, which shows the width of the ε-neighborhood. Along the bottom edge, semi-transparent grey dots represent i.i.d. samples. Several dots fall inside each shaded band, and others are spread across the axis. A small tick marks the mean at the center. The image is monochrome and uncluttered. The eye goes first to the bell curve, then to the two shaded bands. The image appears to be cropped at the bottom. The axis line and some dots are cut off, and the caption's decoder formula is absent.
caption: Depiction of the $(2, 0, \mathcal{O}(\tfrac{1}{\epsilon} \log \tfrac{1}{\epsilon}))$-sample compression scheme for $\mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$ over $\mathbb{R}$. Given $\mathcal{O}(\tfrac{1}{\epsilon} \log \tfrac{1}{\epsilon}\log\frac{1}{\delta})$ i.i.d. samples from this Gaussian (shown as grey dots), with probability at least $1 - \delta$, there exist two distinct samples, $X_i$ and $X_j$, falling within $\epsilon$-neighborhoods of $\mu - \sigma$ and $\mu + \sigma$, respectively. A simple decoder, defined as $\mathcal{N}\left({(X_i + X_j)}/{2}, {(X_j - X_i)^2}/{4}\right)$, then reconstructs an estimate of the distribution with TV error $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon)$. Importantly, the indices $i$ and $j$ need not be known — it suffices that such samples exist within the dataset.
abstract: Learning distribution families over $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a fundamental problem in unsupervised learning and statistics. A central question in this setting is whether a given family of distributions possesses sufficient structure to be (at least) information-theoretically learnable and, if so, to characterize its sample complexity. In 2018, Ashtiani et al. (2018) reformulated sample compressibility as a structural property of distribution classes, proving that it guarantees PAC-learnability. This discovery subsequently enabled a series of recent advancements in deriving nearly tight sample complexity bounds for various high-dimensional open problems. It has been further conjectured that the converse also holds: every learnable class admits a sample compression scheme, making the two notions to be equivalent. In this work, we establish that sample compressible families remain learnable even from perturbed samples, subject to a set of minimax-necessary and sufficient conditions. In particular, we assume samples are corrupted by an additive independent noise model, and theoretically derive sample complexity bounds for general sample compressible classes in arbitrary dimensions with respect to both $\ell_2$-norm and total variation distance.
